text:
There are a few things we can enhance. First, make the input device detection automatic rather than fixed. In the settings, there should be an option to change the microphone, but on the onboarding page, it should auto-detect and also provide an option to add or change the input device directly. Currently, the input device is fixed, so users cannot change it or add an option there to auto-detect their specific device. Additionally, add a horizontal bar to show volume detection, making it noticeable that the volume is being detected while speaking. Replace the green light circular blinking effect with audio waveforms on the green dots, but do not remove the existing effect; just add the waveform effect. Apply the same changes to the onboarding page.

Next, remove the three dots, specifically the red, yellow, and green indicators, and do not do anything else with that section for now. We can talk about that later. Also, remove the GitHub and docs links from the about page. While private and local features are present, they are not the main feature, so we cannot market it as such. However, it is fine to leave that information at the bottom for version 1, so do not change that. Finally, make the hotkey customizable, as it is currently not customizable.

It's not like it's a typeable thing, so I don't think that's good. Make that fix and we are good to go. When they press it, they should have an option to choose their key combination. So whenever they press the keyboard, they can choose the combination, and escape cancels it, leading to the default, which is control space. Right. As for audio, like advanced, remove all those. I think okay, let it be; that's fine, we can check. All right, history works fine, everything works fine, so the basic app is ready. So change all this, we are good to go then.

Also, add guidance so people can understand which model to choose, like in the Groq cloud search provider. Have an option that names the models so we can understand which is faster, which is better, and what each one does. This is really important because normally people would choose larger models like Large V3, and it takes more time to transcribe, making them think the app is slow. So let them know by having transcription settings separately in the sidebar. When they click, they can see the models and cleanup mode in detail, explaining what they actually do, rather than having it buried in the general settings. That's one thing you can do, and we are good to go. I can't change the UI at all; the existing design is fine. Everything should be preserved, including the design. This is version one, which is ready. Let's do it, and we are good to go.

I really like the work that has been done in Astra, so I want to merge it with master. I want to keep everything from the Astra branch because it is end-to-end and everything works properly in that commit. For anything that conflicts or is different in master, remove that and keep the Astra version. We are good to commit this now. Do a merge commit with a message like "Production ready UI version 1" or "Finalized UI." Merge Astra with the master branch, and if there are any conflicts, resolve them by removing the master code. I want everything in my master branch to be as good as it is in the Astra branch.

Can you increase the canvas size itself? Okay, this is good and this is exactly what I need, but can you increase the exact canvas size so I can extract each element individually and still have the highest quality for those individual elements? That is the main goal here. If you give me a canvas size of 140 by 140 pixels, and I extract a small element out of it, it would be way too small and unusable for a UI element in my website or app. So I want you to give me a canvas of 5,000 by 5,000 pixels and then generate all the images according to what was said in the above prompt. Yes, please do it for me.

It was really fast, but now it has become really slow. It's taking a lot of time; it was instant in the US, literally instantly working before we began the UI changes and started with the main files. When we fixed it, it worked at a snap—as I just tapped my hotkey, it was ready to paste in just one second, maybe even not even one second. But now it's taking four, five, six, maybe 10 seconds to process and then paste, which is a lot of time. So can you fix that error? There are a few more changes I want to make.

Make the app draggable and movable. The app is currently fixed at one position, and I cannot drag or move it. In the transcription page, stop the horizontal scroll; I don't need horizontal scroll. Describe everything within the layout without horizontal scrolling. Make the left bar, which has the settings, transcription history, and all, collapsible so it collapses and I can work with more space. When collapsed, the text should also collapse, only making the logos visible. Don't have any horizontal scroll for anything; that's not looking good.

One more thing I want to change is the hotkey. It's okay with Control Space, but remove the click-to-change option. Just have Control Space, but the button should have some background blur or something so it looks different and feels clickable. We are good there. Then, center out the text; remove the arrows and all draggable things. In the history size, just have a text box that fits the text with no extra spaces, and it should be centrally aligned.

On the onboarding page, make the waveforms of the mic actually align with the input of the mic. It should detect the input and then align with that, so the waveforms are designed to actually work. It should not only blink; it should at least show waveforms going up and down. Improve the speed of it. That's the first thing: first things first, improve the speed. Even in the fast engine and the cloud engine, this is going very slow.

Remove the high-speed online transcription 300 milliseconds link; we don't need that. But have an on-device engine which has returned something like 100% private. For the cloud engine, have something with smaller return text so that we can collapse it and use less space. Yeah, and we are good to go. Consider everything and then first map out the task whatever I said and do it, because every task is important; don't miss anything. So yeah, get this all done. We are good to go then. And that's it.

Also, check where the issue is coming from, what the issue is, and why this is happening. Explain it to me in a short, simple manner so I can understand it, and tell me how we are going to fix it. Remember how we did it in the previous sessions and how we fixed it so that it becomes really instantaneous. It was really instant; as soon as I tapped the button, the transcript was ready to paste. I need that level of speed. Even with the larger model, there was just a 1 to 1.5-second delay, and it was already done. For larger prompts and larger inputs, it was always even better. For smaller inputs, it usually took the same small amount of time as the larger inputs. That was the case in the previous setup, but I don't know what has changed. Make it happen and make it the same. However, do not compromise on any formatting or cleaning, because everything looks really good. Do not compromise this for the sake of speed. The speed should come by itself, even while doing all this.
